summary: Full regression after the Postgres to MongoDB migration plus the new Emergent object storage uploads. Backend: wrote new pymongo-based pytest suite (25 tests) covering public events/projects (seeded 3+3 present, scopes), bookings (201/409/400 capacity/422), member registration (GIG-<year>-NNNN increments, 409, 422), auth (httpOnly cookies, me/refresh/logout, bcrypt $2b$, 5 fails -> 429, 'Password non ancora impostata', admin register domain check + verify-email flow, set/change/forgot password), member dashboard + 403 on admin, admin stats/members/fees/resend/delete/contacts/events CRUD (Europe/Rome tz, end<start 400)/bookings/projects CRUD, uploads (401 anon, 403 member, 400 wrong type, 400 >8MB, 201 url, GET returns identical bytes with image/png, unknown 404). 25/25 pass. CORS returns explicit origin + credentials. Frontend: admin login -> /admin, Nuovo evento modal upload fills image field + preview loads, saved event shows uploaded image on /eventi card and detail; same for project modal, /progetti list and /progetti/<slug>; unsupported file shows toast 'Formato non supportato'. Smoke: home (no broken images), booking-success, membership-success, all 5 admin pages load. All test data cleaned (files marked is_deleted=true).

minor.issue: Lockout identifier uses the first X-Forwarded-For value, which the client controls (a spoofed XFF value was honoured in the tests). An attacker can rotate the header to get around the 5-attempt lockout. Use the ingress-appended (last) hop, or also lock per email.

The capacity check runs before the duplicate check, so someone already booked on a full event gets 400 'Evento al completo' instead of 409. The count-then-insert capacity check is not atomic, so concurrent requests can overbook.
Only the client-supplied content_type is validated; there is no magic-byte check. The whole body is read into memory before the 8MB check.
upcoming_events also counts unpublished events (no is_published filter).
The email provider returned 'rate_limited' after many test sends, so email_sent=false. This is handled gracefully and is not a code bug.

issues: Inizio/Fine use the browser's native datetime-local picker (mm/dd/yyyy US format shown), which does not match the themed UI

action_items: Optional hardening: do not trust a client-supplied first X-Forwarded-For for the login lockout key
Optional: check for duplicate bookings before capacity, and make the capacity check atomic
Optional: check image magic bytes on upload
Optional: filter stats upcoming_events by is_published
critical_code_review_comments: routers/auth.py _client_ip trusts the left-most XFF value, which lets clients bypass the brute-force lockout
routers/events.py book_event has a capacity race condition, and a duplicate booking on a full event gets the wrong error code
routers/files.py has no signature sniffing and does a full read before the size check
Deleting an event or project does not mark its uploaded file is_deleted (orphan files; minor)

Lockout test uses a random X-Forwarded-For. Console 401s in the UI come from the anonymous /auth/me bootstrap (expected).
